title: Invariance of the inactive row frame
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, and let $x$ and $y$ be Boolean words. Let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on input $y$, let $b$ be a Boolean tag, and let $n$ assign a natural number to each of the $2(1+M.k)$ counter fields. Choose two record words, two control states of the row-copying machine with $2(1+M.k)$ work tapes, natural numbers $T$ and $t$, and a configuration $z$ of that row-copying machine on input $x$. Relocating $z$ into the row's designated tapes while retaining the other tape contents and head positions gives the same configuration for either choice of record word and row control state.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite-state Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
$c$ is a configuration of $M$ on input $y$
$n$ assigns a natural number to each of the $2(1+M.k)$ counter fields
the row controls are states of the row-copying machine
$z$ is a configuration of the row-copying machine on input $x
replaced: For every source configuration, tag, movement counts, clock budget, and logical time, the retained inactive tapes and heads used when relocating a row-copy configuration into the recorder are the same for any two record contents and row controls, so consecutive fields and rows can append to the record without changing source time.
